title: Iraqi potters make a polychrome luster bowl
summary: A glazed earthenware bowl attributed to ninth-century Iraq combines ruby-colored and golden luster around a large palmette design.

citations.locator: Object 22.49.1; Date, Geography, Medium and opening description
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: A glazed earthenware bowl attributed to ninth-century Iraq combines ruby-colored and golden luster around a large palmette design.
The catalogue gives only the ninth century. The range marks uncertainty about one object’s manufacture, not a century-long production task.
The museum’s attribution concerns this surviving bowl. Its decorated surface provides material evidence of polychrome luster painting, without identifying an individual potter.

review.corroboration: The Met object’s description and catalogue fields were compared. No independent workshop attribution or narrower dating was established.
